title: Constant coefficients, locality, and domain property of a completed positive monoid algebra
statement:
Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonzero Noetherian local commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], complete and separated for the powers of $\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Let $P$ be a finitely generated additive submonoid of a free abelian group $G\cong\mathbf Z^r$, where $r\ge0$, and let $w:G	o\mathbf Z$ be a homomorphism strictly positive on $P\setminus\{0\}$. Write $A[P]= igoplus_{p\in P}Az^p$, with $z^pz^q=z^{p+q}$, set $\mathfrak b=(\mathfrak m,z^p:p
e0)$ and $B=\varprojlim_n A[P]/\mathfrak b^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Put $J=(z^p:p
e0)B$. The constant-coefficient map on $A[P]$ extends to a surjective $A$-algebra homomorphism $c:B	o A$. Under the coefficient-family identification $B\cong A^P$ with finite convolution multiplication, this map sends $(a_p)$ to $a_0$. Its kernel is $J$, and it induces the canonical $A$-algebra isomorphism $B/J\cong A$. An element $f\in B$ is a unit if and only if $c(f)$ is a unit of $A$. The ring $B$ is local, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n=c^{-1}(\mathfrak m)=\mathfrak bB$ and residue field $A/\mathfrak m$. If $A$ is an integral domain (that is, $1
e0$ and a product of two nonzero elements is nonzero), then $B$ is an integral domain. For $P=\{0\}$ these maps identify $B$ with $A$ and $J$ with $0$.

source.place: VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70, agent-supplied coefficient-algebra refinement: constant-coefficient kernel, geometric-series locality, and least-monomial domain argument (old proof steps 3--4 of lem-trf-formal-monoid-ring-dimension).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-monoid-completion-coefficients] with precisely the given $A,P,G,w,\mathfrak b$. Its completeness and finite-generation hypotheses are among ours. Identify $B$ with $A^P$ by its $A$-algebra isomorphism; multiplication is finite convolution and the image of $az^p$ is the family supported at $p$ with coefficient $a$.

source.place: VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70: agent-written coefficient-algebra refinement, not a theorem stated in ILO.

proof.text: Define $c(f)=f_0$. If $u+v=0$ in $P$, then $w(u)+w(v)=0$ and strict positivity forces $u=v=0$. Consequently $(fg)_0=f_0g_0$; addition and the unit are preserved coefficientwise. Thus $c$ is an $A$-algebra homomorphism extending the polynomial constant coefficient. Writing $C(a)=az^0$, one has $c(C(a))=a$, so $c$ is surjective.

source.place: VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70: agent-written coefficient-algebra refinement, not a theorem stated in ILO.

proof.text: Choose nonzero monoid generators $g_1,\ldots,g_s$, with $s=0$ permitted. Every nonzero $p$ has $\nu(p)\ge1$, whereas $\nu(0)=0$. For $f_0=0$, apply [lem-trf-high-length-prefix-division] at $n=1$: it expresses $f=f^{\ge1}$ as the finite sum $\sum_{i=1}^s z^{g_i}c^i$, so $f\in J$. Conversely every generator $z^p$ of $J$ has constant coefficient zero, hence $J\subseteq\ker c$. Therefore $\ker c=J$. The induced map $B/J\to A$ has inverse $a\mapsto C(a)+J$: for $f\in B$, $f-C(c(f))\in J$, which verifies the other inverse identity. Both maps preserve the $A$-algebra structure.

source.place: VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70: agent-written coefficient-algebra refinement, not a theorem stated in ILO.

proof.text: If $f$ is a unit then $c(f)$ is a unit by applying $c$ to an inverse. Conversely put $a=c(f)\in A^\times$ and $h=1-C(a^{-1})f$, so $h_0=0$. The finite convolution formula, by induction on $k$, gives $(h^k)_p=0$ for $k>w(p)$: each nonzero summand requires $k$ nonzero exponents whose positive integer weights sum to $w(p)$. Define the family $s_p=\sum_{k=0}^{w(p)}(h^k)_p$. It belongs to $A^P=B$, without any convergence assertion. For a fixed $p$, all pairs $u+v=p$ are finite, and $w(u),w(v)\le w(p)$. Thus in computing $((1-h)s)_p$ one may replace $s$ by $\sum_{k=0}^{w(p)}h^k$. The polynomial identity $(1-h)\sum_{k=0}^Nh^k=1-h^{N+1}$ and the same support bound give $((1-h)s)_p=1_p$. Hence $fC(a^{-1})s=1$, giving the required inverse.

source.place: VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70: agent-written coefficient-algebra refinement, not a theorem stated in ILO.

proof.text: By the unit criterion, the nonunits of $B$ are exactly $\mathfrak n=c^{-1}(\mathfrak m)$, a proper ideal. Every proper ideal contains only nonunits, hence is contained in $\mathfrak n$; this proves locality and that $\mathfrak n$ is the unique maximal ideal. For $f\in\mathfrak n$, $f=C(c(f))+(f-C(c(f)))$ with the first term in $\mathfrak m B$ and the second in $J$. The reverse inclusion follows by applying $c$, so $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak mB+J=\mathfrak bB$. Explicit inverse maps between $B/\mathfrak n$ and $A/\mathfrak m$ are $f+\mathfrak n\mapsto c(f)+\mathfrak m$ and $a+\mathfrak m\mapsto C(a)+\mathfrak n$. This identifies the residue field.

source.place: VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70: agent-written coefficient-algebra refinement, not a theorem stated in ILO.

proof.text:
Now assume $A$ is a domain. Choose coordinates $G\cong\mathbf Z^r$ and order $P$ lexicographically by $(w(p),p_1,\ldots,p_r)$. This is a total order preserved by translation. Each nonempty subset of $P$ has a least element: take its least nonnegative integer weight, then its least element in that finite weight fibre; finiteness follows from [lem-trf-positive-monoid-adic-filtration]. For nonzero $f,g\in A^P$ let $p,q$ be their least supported exponents. If $f_ug_v
e0$, then $u\ge p$ and $v\ge q$. Translation invariance makes $u+v>p+q$ if either inequality is strict. Thus the only nonzero summand in the finite convolution at $p+q$ is $f_pg_q
e0$. Hence $fg
e0$. Also $C(1)_0=1
e0$, so $B$ is nonzero and is an integral domain.

source.place: VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70: agent-written coefficient-algebra refinement, not a theorem stated in ILO.

proof.text: When $P=\{0\}$ the coefficient-family isomorphism is $B\cong A^{\{0\}}=A$, and $c$ and $C$ are its inverse maps. There are no nonconstant monomials, so $J=0$; the inverse formula reduces to $s=1$ and all preceding identifications specialize to these maps.

source.place: VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70: agent-written coefficient-algebra refinement, not a theorem stated in ILO.
